objective: Publish one reproducible, machine-generated multi-scenario software readiness report that records the commit and configuration hashes a clean checkout reproduces, lists every registered scenario identity with its tests, replay hash, evidence completeness, failure coverage, release eligibility and known limitations, separates software, scripted-fixture, Gazebo and physical evidence statuses, and refuses to render NOT_EXECUTED, BLOCKED or release_eligible: false as a success.
decision_supported: Whether a release can point at one generated artifact that states, per registered scenario identity, what the software is ready for and what was never executed, instead of a hand-written table that could claim a physical validation this checkout cannot support.
acceptance: the report lists every registered scenario identity from the live registry, so a scenario added without regenerating the report fails the gate rather than silently missing a row

each row records the scenario identity, evidence status, its own evidence class (software, scripted_fixture, gazebo, physical), release_eligible, the verifier entry point, the recovery policy, the required adapters, the conformance dimensions it proves, the failure paths covered and its known limitations, with every generated field marked as generated and a stated prohibition on hand-editing a test outcome, hash or eligibility

the four evidence classes are independent axes: a scripted fixture is recorded as scripted_fixture and never as software or physical success, and NOT_EXECUTED, BLOCKED and release_eligible false are never rendered as a pass

the report records the commit it was generated from and a configuration hash over the registry, contract, conformance corpus and matrix inputs, so a clean checkout regenerates a byte-identical report and a changed input changes the hash

the gate recomputes the report from the committed inputs and fails when the committed artifact is stale, when a registered identity has no row, when a row claims an evidence class stronger than its manifest, or when a generated field was hand-edited
the README capability and evidence table is generated from the same data, so the published table cannot disagree with the machine-readable report

the report and gate are read-only for every other module: they import the registry, the conformance reader and the eligibility predicate rather than reimplementing them, start no simulator, write no run or event and claim no physical validation
the gate is wired into the required foundation-checks job and the local make check chain, so an unregenerated report fails CI rather than a reviewer's memory
evidence: pytest transcript for tests/unit/test_readiness_report.py with the passed count and collected test names
the generated docs/evaluation/readiness-report-v1.json showing every registered identity, its evidence class, release_eligible and configuration hash
the gate output for the committed report, plus its refusal output for a stale report, a missing row and a hand-edited outcome
the generated markdown table and README capability table showing a scripted fixture rendered as scripted_fixture and never as software or physical success
full-suite pytest output with passed and skipped counts, ruff check and ruff format output, make context-check output and git diff --check output
stop_conditions: the change would require editing interfaces/, libs/contracts/ or another path that needs three human approvals
the change would require a schema amendment, a Pydantic model change or a new runtime dependency
the change would require a physical, Gazebo or HIL claim, or require an executed external run to produce the report
the change would require editing a frozen scenario, a seed, a scene hash or a registry manifest
the change would require the report to infer a test outcome it did not run
a required modification falls outside allowed_paths
data_classification: public repository source, documentation and committed scripted test fixtures; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may write the report generator, the gate, the committed generated artifact, the README table and the tests; a named human Owner accepts the evidence vocabulary and owns the release decision the report informs
risks_and_fallbacks: the report could be read as a release approval; fallback is that it states the evidence class per scenario and that it grants no release or physical-validation authority, and the gate refuses a stronger class than the manifest supports
a generated table could drift from the artifact; fallback is that the README table and the markdown page are generated from the same committed JSON and the gate recomputes both
a scenario could be registered without a row; fallback is that the gate derives the identity set from the live registry and fails a missing row by identity
the configuration hash could be unstable across machines; fallback is that it hashes canonical sorted JSON of the named inputs and a test asserts two generations in one checkout agree
rollback is a revert of this commit; the report, the gate and the table are additive and no fixture, seed, manifest or runtime path changes
